text.p: New Zealand snatched a semifinal place from second-seeded Australia by crushing their Pacific neighbours 3-0 in the Alfred Dunhill Cup on Saturday.

With Frank Nobilo holding off a charging Greg Norman on the final green to preserve a 66-68 victory, seventh-seeded New Zealand completed an improbable whitewash to take a place in the last four against third-seeded South Africa.
It was the third successive year that Australia have dropped their third round robin group tie 3-0 and each time it has cost them a place in the final four.
In the other matches in the tie, Grant Waite beat Wayne Riley 69-76 and Greg Turner defeated Steve Elkington 69-73.
Australia, who won their first two ties, would have gone through if they had won just one of the three matches.
South Africa progressed when Wayne Westner shot a sparkling birdie three at the 17th hole of his decisive match against Ireland's Padraig Harrington.
The top-seeded United States beat Spain 3-0 and in the other semifinal will face unseeded Sweden, who ended the dream of the Indian team, who beat Scotland on Friday, by defeating them 3-0.
Nobilo birdied five of the first seven holes against Norman to go three ahead. But from four in front with four holes to play he led by only one playing the last.
Norman struck back with birdies at the 15th and 17th, where he hit his 190-yard five-iron to three feet to rival Westner's equally superb shot earlier.
Nobilo bogeyed the 17th. But from the last fairway, Norman finished 15 feet from the flag before Nobilo hit his second shot from 76 yards to just two feet.
"From 70-80 yards I'm usually pretty bad," Nobilo said.
"This was a good win for me but it would not have meant anything if the others guys had not won their matches."
Nobilo had a bit of good fortune at the 10th where he hit his tee shot wide of the fairway. He hit a provisional ball, but then found the first, took a penalty drop and got away with a bogey five.
"That was a good break for him but he played superbly. All the New Zealand boys did," Norman said.
"Frank's wonderful second shot at the last closed the door."
Turner, who has lost his last seven Dunhill Cup matches over three years, was delighted to contribute to the team success.
He had expected to be picked for the team ahead of Waite based on rankings, but was not, then needed the withdrawal of Michael Campbell to have a place on the team.
"I was not too happy about all of that but the way it has worked out it is my good fortune," he said.
Waite, based on the U.S. Tour, has won all three of his games.

Westner's great shot at the 17th set up a 69-70 victory over Padraig Harrington of Ireland, but his heroics were matched by Retief Goosen, who had dropped his first two games with scores of 78 and 76.

He abandoned his driver to hit irons off the tee, giving 50 yards away on each hole to Darren Clarke yet still matched the Irishman's 70 and beat him with a 20-foot birdie putt on the first playoff hole.
It was just as well, with world number four Ernie Els going down in his match 69-71 to Paul McGinley.
The U.S. team of Phil Mickelson, Mark O'Meara and Steve Stricker won in a canter over Spain with victorious rounds of 66, 67 and 70 respectively.
Sweden took the other final semifinal place with their triumph over the unheralded debutants from India, who had upset defending champions Scotland on Friday.
